request_summary: Read the review comments on the GEC pull request, plan the fixes, then apply them using the AFM oracle for issuer fixtures and a 5-second timeout.

actions.description: Read the six inline review comments and confirmed each against the code; produced a fix plan with owners, decisions and risks.

Compared the issuer fixture procedure with the AFM oracle (delete by partition, then create, no restore) and routed the work: utility engineer, QA engineer and QA analyst in parallel, then a second engineer round for the strict-cardinality step.

The utility engineer returned a plan only because its harness was read-only; under the human's authorization the orchestrator applied the utility change directly (lazy annotations, pinned azure-data-tables, blob README).

Verified: reproduced the TableEntity NameError on Python 3.13 with the original file and confirmed the fixed file imports; py_compile of the changed Python files; confirmed each new/changed step text matches exactly one registered step; reviewed the engineer diff, reverted a whitespace-only change and removed a duplicated partition constant.
Assessed README impact: GEC and blob READMEs already updated by the change set; root and utility READMEs need no change.

outcome.detail: All six review points are implemented and statically verified; no Behave run was performed, so runtime behavior (notably the stricter full-cardinality assertions) is unverified.

notes: Strict cardinality may expose failures in gec_002_01/02/07 (scenarios with no PSP filter). The oracle deletes whole partitions without restoring; the GEC suite keeps that procedure and adds a best-effort snapshot and restore. Python-utility-engineer is not a configured ACE participant, so no trace was written for it. Nothing was committed or pushed.

friction.description: The Python-utility-engineer harness was read-only and could not edit or run commands; the orchestrator applied its plan directly after explicit human authorization.

The QA-engineer could not execute commands, so its changes were verified by the orchestrator after the fact; the engineer also left a whitespace-only edit and removed blank lines between decorated functions, which were corrected.
Early gh api calls using a multi-value jq filter failed and the search tool named in the instructions was unavailable; PowerShell JSON parsing and Select-String were used instead.
